beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals is engaged in processing and selling specialty chemicals organized into four categories: Functional Additives (FA), Chemically Modified Minerals (CMM), Soft Minerals (SM) and Hard Minerals (HM).
The company has a long-term arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, to market and sell its products through the promoter's network — a key dependency.
Top 10 customers accounted for around 59%, 57% and 59% of revenue from operations in FY2015, FY2016 and FY2017 respectively, indicating moderate customer concentration.
The company exports to Nigeria, Saudi Arabia and Sri Lanka, with exports totalling ₹1,068.18 lakh over the past five years.

Competitive strengths listed in the DRHP include a diversified product portfolio, diversified user industries, import substitution potential, support from the holding company, and product innovation through continuous R&D.

beats.beat: Profit after tax (PAT) turned positive from FY2015 onwards after two loss-making years: ₹(27.40) lakh in FY2013, ₹(12.17) lakh in FY2014, then ₹149.58 lakh in FY2015, ₹90.18 lakh in FY2016, ₹174.82 lakh in FY2017, and ₹132.75 lakh for the six months ended September 30, 2017.
Basic earnings per share (EPS) followed the same trajectory: (₹0.45) in FY2013, (₹0.20) in FY2014, then ₹2.47, ₹1.46, ₹2.43 for FY2015–2017, and ₹1.48 for the six months ended September 2017.

Cash flow from operations was negative in FY2014 at (₹349.75) lakh but turned positive in subsequent periods: ₹802.59 lakh in FY2015, ₹422.36 lakh in FY2016, ₹127.73 lakh in FY2017, and ₹200.97 lakh for the six months ended September 30, 2017.
Total assets grew from ₹2,679.38 lakh as at March 31, 2013 to ₹3,424.96 lakh as at September 30, 2017.
Revenue from operations and debt details were not available in the extracted facts.

beats.beat: Promoters of the company are Mr. Chandresh S. Parikh, Mr. Atil C. Parikh, Mr. Rajesh C. Parikh and 20 Microns Limited (the corporate promoter).
Promoters collectively hold 89,48,270 equity shares, representing 99.76% of the pre-issue paid-up equity share capital.
The promoter group (excluding promoters) holds 21,510 equity shares, or 0.24% of the pre-issue paid-up capital.
Related party transactions have occurred during the last five financial years and the six-month period ended September 30, 2017, as per Accounting Standard 18.

Governance flags include: instances of non-filings or delays in filing statutory forms with the RoC (since rectified with additional fees); lack of registration for the corporate logo; and not owning the premises for two manufacturing facilities and two administrative offices.
The company, promoters, group companies and directors are parties to certain legal proceedings, any adverse outcome of which could materially affect the business.

beats.beat: The specialty chemicals segment (excluding agrochemicals and dyestuff) was estimated at roughly ₹1,000 billion in fiscal 2017, with the overall Indian chemicals industry (excluding pharma and fertilisers) at ₹5,800–6,200 billion.
CRISIL Research estimated that the specialty chemicals segment grew at 10–12% CAGR from fiscal 2014 to 2017 and is forecast to grow at 12–14% CAGR going forward.
The industry is highly fragmented: small and medium enterprises hold 70–75% market share; only a few Indian players can compete with global giants on product development.

Key demand drivers include rising consumption, improved living standards, government initiatives (draft National Chemical Policy, 100% FDI allowed), and favourable global shifts such as China's stricter environmental regulations reducing its specialty chemical output.

Within specialty chemicals, sub-segments are projected to grow at varying rates: construction chemicals and water chemicals at 15% CAGR, polymer additives at 10% CAGR, and textiles at 12% CAGR, among others.

Regulations relevant to the sector include the REACH regime for exports to Europe, GST implementation from July 1, 2017, and the government's four Petroleum, Chemicals and Petrochemicals Investment Regions (PCPIRs) with proposed investments of about ₹9 trillion.

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals Limited processes and sells specialty chemicals — functional additives and chemically modified minerals — and relies on its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, to market and sell its products through their network.
The company is raising capital through an SME IPO on NSE EMERGE, with Vivro Financial Services Private Limited as the lead manager and Link Intime India Private Limited as the registrar.

The issue is a fresh issue of equity shares; the objects include funding capital expenditure for a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat, and general corporate purposes.
As of September 30, 2017, the company had an issued, subscribed and paid-up capital of ₹897.00 lakh (89,70,000 equity shares of ₹10 each).

beats.beat: The IPO is a fresh issue of equity shares for listing on the SME Platform of NSE (NSE EMERGE). No offer for sale has been disclosed.
Lead manager: Vivro Financial Services Private Limited.
Registrar: Link Intime India Private Limited.

The objects of the issue are: (i) funding capital expenditure for a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat; (ii) general corporate purposes; and (iii) creating a public trading market for the equity shares and enhancing visibility.
The price band and number of shares offered have not been disclosed in the DRHP excerpts.

beats.beat: No long-term agreements with customers or suppliers: The company relies on purchase orders for sales and has no definitive agreements for raw material supply, exposing it to volume, pricing and availability shocks.
Negative cash flows in past years: The company experienced negative operating cash flows in FY2014 (₹349.75 lakh outflow), and sustained negative cash flows could impact growth and business.

Missing statutory licenses for one manufacturing facility: At Plot 9–10, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat, the company has not yet obtained certain required licenses and risks penalties for non-compliance.
Dependence on corporate promoter for marketing: The long-term arrangement with 20 Microns Limited is critical; any disruption could materially affect sales.
Contingent liabilities of ₹29.11 lakh as of September 30, 2017, which if materialized could adversely affect financial condition.
